subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should non-zero process exits remain errors by default, with warning suppression limited to exit codes explicitly marked as accepted by the exec result contract?
rationale: The runtime's `completed` status only confirms normal process termination, so source inspection cannot determine which non-zero codes the product should treat as successful without an explicit semantic contract.

options.title: Add explicit accepted exits
options.body: Keep generic non-zero failures visible and suppress warnings only when the exec result explicitly marks the exit code as accepted.

options.title: Suppress all completed exits
options.body: Adopt this PR's interpretation that every normally terminated process is non-error, accepting that genuine command failures may become quiet.

options.title: Retain current behavior
options.body: Keep all non-zero exits classified as errors and close the linked request unless a narrower contract is sponsored.

recommendation.title: Add explicit accepted exits
recommendation.body: Keep generic non-zero failures visible and suppress warnings only when the exec result explicitly marks the exit code as accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The behavior appears tied most directly to the user-facing tool-error warning path introduced in `dbdc0eb`.
